To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
machine learning can be used to classify sentences in a legal text, but that the resulting model does not generalize as well as a pattern-based approach.

the machine learning approach performs as accurate as the pattern-based approach, that the pattern based approach generalizes better to new legislation, that the machine learning based approach can be used to find patterns that are useful for the pattern based approach and that the machine learning classifier is more robust to errors in the data.
the ML classifier performs well on the training data, but does not generalize as well as the pattern-based classifier.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether ML can be used as a substitute for knowledge based classification.
the question whether it is possible to replace a pattern based classification approach with an ML approach.
the use of ML for classification of legal texts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ML techniques can be useful in the context of legal text classification, but only if they are used in a complementary manner to pattern-based classification.

the pattern based approach should be used for the first round of classification, while ML techniques are to be preferred for the second round, in which a small number of misclassified sentences is to be resolved.
ML techniques are a valuable addition to the arsenal of tools available to legal experts, but should not be seen as a substitute for the human expert.

the use of ML for classification of legal texts is not yet mature.

the use of machine learning techniques in the field of legislation classification is promising, but that more research is needed to make these techniques useful for real world applications.

ML techniques are not yet suitable to replace the knowledge-based classification of legal texts.
machine learning is a useful tool to improve the accuracy of a classifier, but the results are not always better than those from the pattern-based approach.
